summary: Validated (the first patch attempt failed on malformed hunk headers and was re-issued cleanly; validate --run <run> --submission update28.json → valid=true). Closed the coverage question for the VerifyLeader finding. Every retained verification test builds an all-voter cluster: three voters with all links up expecting success (raft_test.go:1866-1881); a single-node case taking the quorum-of-one shortcut; two voters where the follower is forced to a higher term and verification must fail with a leadership error (1900-1938); and three voters where one follower is disconnected and success is still expected (1940-1971). The membership tests that add non-voting members never call verification, so no retained expectation addresses how acknowledgements from a non-voter are treated — the mixed-suffrage case is untested in either direction. One useful positive detail, recorded honestly in the opposite direction: the partial-connect test fixes the expectation that one unreachable member among three voters still yields success, which is exactly the behaviour of counting acknowledgements up to the voter quorum — the same counting that, when the acknowledgements come from non-voters, satisfies the threshold without voter contact. So the suite pins the arithmetic but never varies the suffrage mix, which is why the recorded evidence-source gap survived the tests. Recorded as one Fact plus an 'explained' interpretation for a new coverage question, with counterevidence preserved (the partial-connect case does constrain the all-voter case; the failure test covers the opposite direction; a coverage gap is not evidence about the mixed case, whose support remains the separately recorded code paths) and the explicit caveat that the tests were read, not run.
